extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and selling points used to describe and evaluate a university journalism program (what makes a strong program / what students should expect to gain). Focused on BU College of Communication's journalism offerings and experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Students learn journalism by doing it: cover Boston’s neighborhoods, courts, and city hall while building a real portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join the Massachusetts Statehouse program, jump to Washington, DC for more experience, or take international opportunities. Emphasizes practical beat reporting that results in a portfolio of published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional-level newsroom and editing suites
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to professional-level newsroom and editing suites for training and production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use industry-standard facilities and studios to produce work that is publishable/airable; training in these spaces is presented as a core part of the education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report in a top media market
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities to report in the heart of a top 10 U.S. media market (Boston).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proximity to a major media market is framed as a practical advantage for newsroom experience, local reporting, and connections to outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-run and professional publishing outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple in-house and local outlets where students can file pieces: BU News Service, WTBU Radio, BUTV10, the Daily Free Press, and local news outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outlets provide regular, real-world publishing and broadcasting opportunities that serve as training grounds and portfolio builders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-winning faculty and alumni
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty include Pulitzer and Emmy winners; alumni are award-winning professionals working at major outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty are active in industry and highly connected; alumni networks and mentors are presented as pathways to professional development and jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documented journalism awards & rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: Program and students regularly win awards (regional Emmys, National Student Production Awards, Pulitzers) and program rankings (e.g., No. 2 College Factual, No. 3 PrepScholar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and external rankings are used as signals of program quality and student success; specific awards and counts (e.g., 21 Pulitzer winners among faculty/alumni) are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong career outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: High placement/outcome rate for graduates (96% of BS in Journalism alumni are employed, in school, or in another chosen activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome statistics are highlighted to demonstrate the program’s effectiveness at launching careers; a link to 'see more outcomes' is provided for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of degree programs and certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal degree offerings: BS in Journalism, MS in Journalism, and Graduate Certificate in Civic Science Communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear program tracks for undergraduate and graduate study and a certificate option indicate curricular breadth and specialization opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Newsroom program (external partnerships)
rubrics_metrics.description: An innovative program that pairs BU COM student reporters with news outlets in Greater Boston to bolster local journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational partnership model: students work with real outlets, suggesting experiential learning and community-engaged reporting experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statehouse Program (state-level politics reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on Massachusetts politics alongside a veteran press corps as part of degree programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-the-beat political reporting experience with professional press corps exposure; positions students to learn statehouse coverage conventions and routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Washington, DC Multimedia & Journalism Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Semester program in Washington, DC to cover Congress or federal agencies for hometown outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extended off-campus semester giving students federal-level reporting experience and bylines for local outlets; useful for students seeking national politics/reporting experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Health Storytelling Fellowship (field reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship in partnership with the Pulitzer Center for field reporting on stories that matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunity for funded, in-the-field reporting on global health topics; emphasizes high-impact, externally partnered reporting experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italy Padua Conflict & Crisis Reporting (international conflict reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer program in Padua, Italy focused on reporting on war, migration, and humanitarian crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term immersive international program led alongside seasoned journalists covering conflict across Europe and the Mediterranean; emphasizes safety-aware conflict and crisis reporting training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice Media co-Lab (data-driven investigative collaborations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For-credit, application-only course pairing journalism majors with Computing & Data Sciences students to produce data-driven investigations for major outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces investigative work for outlets such as the Boston Globe, GBH, ProPublica, MarketWatch, and CBS Boston; highlights interdisciplinary collaboration and real-world investigative production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events and professional convenings (Power of Narrative Conference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual conference bringing together top journalists and authors to explore long-form storytelling craft and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferences and events are positioned as opportunities for learning, networking, and exposure to evolving storytelling practices in long-form journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alumni placement at major media organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Alumni work at top outlets (New York Times, NPR, CNN, Boston Globe, National Geographic) across media platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named alumni and their accomplishments (e.g., Tyler Hicks, Erica Hill, John Terhune) are used as exemplars of career trajectories achievable from the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career pathway breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation for diverse journalism-related careers: newsrooms, documentary production, radio and podcasting, sports media, broadcast and streaming, video editing, photographic journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program emphasizes transferable skills across platforms and formats, suggesting curricular and extracurricular support for varied media careers.
